from_source.claimed_edge: Low-float, high-earnings-growth leaders make explosive trend moves once institutions start accumulating; buying the volume-confirmed breakout of a well-formed base catches the start of that accumulation. The other side: holders selling at the old resistance level, and institutions that buy later at higher prices.

setup_conditions.text: At least 20 bars since the last 20-day closing-high cross, base no deeper than 20%
setup_conditions.quote: Has a well-formed base or pattern with a definable trendline / breakout point

setup_conditions.text: Breakout-day volume at least 2x the 30-day average
setup_conditions.quote: Breakout volume must be above the recent trend - know the stock's 30-day average volume

trigger.quote: Buy as the stock crosses above the trendline / breakout point of the base

exits.text: Sell on any close back below the breakout point
exits.quote: When the break occurs, I am a seller. No questions asked.

exits.text: Exit the remainder on a close below the 20-day average (stands in for his hand-drawn trendline)
exits.quote: Primary sell signal: a break of the support trendline.
Typical holding period 20 minutes to 10 weeks

from_house.survivorship: Survivors-only price cache: the stored universe is today's listed NSE stocks, delisted names are absent, so small-cap results read optimistic.

success_bars.S2: any variant with close-entry PF >= 1.2 in BOTH eras A and B, n >= 150
success_bars.S5: must beat ryan_minervini_book as incumbent or add uncorrelated trades; >= +3%/yr on trading capital after costs

stock_selection.text: Leader: composite RS rank at least 70
stock_selection.quote: Leading group / hot theme - in a strong sector tied to a new technology or trend

chase_limit_pct.quote: Never pay more than 5% above the trendline / breakout point

partial_exits.text: Sell 25% at +17.5% above the pivot (midpoint of his 20-30% at +15-20%)
partial_exits.quote: Sell 20-30% of the position as the stock moves 15-20% above the breakout point

max_hold_bars.quote: 20 minutes to 10 weeks; most trades 6-12 days

good_to_have.pyramiding: Starter position on the breakout; adds heavily only if it 'really blasts off'. Not modelled at S1.

position_sizing_in_source.notes: Record-era sizing was pyramiding + concentration + margin; the '1% risk' rule is a secondhand recap, not his statement.

results.title: Systematic Backtesting & Analysis of Breakout Setups
results.author: e0 (github.com/e0)
results.differences: Not Zanger: prior 50% move in 50 days, ADR >= 3%, 5-40 day consolidation, Theil-Sen trendline breakout; entry at signal-day close; stop at entry-day low; exit on close < SMA10; no volume-explosion leg. Directly relevant to Zanger's scale-out: compares a partial sell against a full exit.
results.universe: tickers listed on base.report (survivorship bias acknowledged by the author)
results.quote: The backtesting results reveal that making full sells at the exit provides significantly better performance compared to selling 50% of the position during the partial sell window.
results.credibility_reason: Rules fully published and 27,500 trades, but no costs, no out-of-sample split, survivorship bias, and 52.69% of trades lost money; +1.76% average is before costs.

external_evaluations.summary: No independent test of Zanger's own rules was found; his record is anecdotal (1998-2000, margin). The closest public evidence is a loose US breakout study: positive pre-cost average trade, and full exits beat 50% partial sells - a reason to also test V1 without the 25% scale-out. Nothing NSE-specific with real data was found.

extras.notes: Results speak about the codable proxy, not the man. The S2 question is whether Zanger's distinctive elements add anything beyond Ryan's already-measured shape.
